claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC dendritic material.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has about 800 MPa room-temperature yield strength.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy exhibits roughly 40% strain at room temperature.
Unmodified TiVNbTa has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Unmodified TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of about 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding carbon and applying a tailored heat treatment to TiVNbTa will induce in-situ TiC precipitation.
The intervention will produce a fine dispersion of TiC particles within the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
TiC precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
TiC precipitates will refine the TiVNbTa microstructure or grain size.
Second-phase TiC strengthening and grain refinement will improve elevated-temperature yield and compressive strengths.
A related NbMoCrTiAl composite containing TiC reinforcement exhibited a significant strength increase.
Small, well-bonded TiC precipitates will help maintain acceptable ductility.
TiC precipitation will not drastically compromise thermal transport.
Modified TiVNbTa will have roughly 50% higher high-temperature yield strength than unmodified TiVNbTa at 1273 K.
Modified TiVNbTa will have roughly 50% higher high-temperature compressive strength than unmodified TiVNbTa at 1273 K.
Modified TiVNbTa will retain acceptable ductility under the stated high-temperature loading conditions.
Modified TiVNbTa will retain acceptable thermal conductivity for heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed effects apply around 1273 K under compressive loading up to 30% strain.
The modified material can remain compatible with the operating limits of both W and CuCrZr.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies roughly a 50% strength increase, whereas the falsification rule uses an ambiguous 20–50% minimum range, so an increase between 20% and 50% could simultaneously miss the stated prediction and pass one interpretation of the falsification threshold.
